reference.title: Dumbbell One Arm Lateral Raise
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Shoulders, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2 s down (Coratella 2020 used 2-0.5-2)

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbell; light: the arm is a long lever
prescription.progression: Add reps, then 1-2 kg; slower lowering

cues.text: Stand tall, feet about hip width, knees soft, ribs down and glutes lightly braced. Dumbbell beside the right thigh, palm in, elbow soft; left hand on the hip.
Breathe out and raise the arm out to the side, a little in front of the body, thumb forward.
Stop at about shoulder height, elbow level with the hand; shoulder down, away from the ear.
Lower slowly in about 2 s; no leaning or swinging.
Brief pause at the side and repeat; switch arms after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning away and swinging the weight up
mistakes.fix: Stand tall, brace the side of the trunk, use a lighter dumbbell.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear
mistakes.fix: Reach the hand long and out; keep the shoulder blade down.
Stop at about 90 degrees; lateral raises above 90 degrees were linked to impingement signs (impingement study 2014).

kinematics.norm: From the side to about 90 degrees (the range used by Coratella 2020); raises above 90 degrees were associated with impingement signs (impingement study 2014)
About 30 degrees in front of the frontal plane (scapular plane; clinical opinion)
Elbow soft, about 10-20 degrees, held constant (clinical opinion)
Upright, no lean away from the dumbbell (clinical opinion)
2 s up, 0.5 s pause, 2 s down in Coratella 2020

sources.title: GymVisual #035512, Dumbbell One Arm Lateral Raise, video (movement reference)
Coratella et al. 2020, an electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)
Characteristics of shoulder impingement in the recreational weight-training population (J Strength Cond Res 2014;28(4):1081-1089, PubMed 24077379)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Pinching at the top: raise only to about 70-80 degrees and keep the thumb up a little.
Balance: hold a post or rack with the free hand.
progressions: Lean-away lateral raise holding a post.
Slower lowering (3 s) or a 2 s hold at the top.

muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Main mover. The lateral raise gave the highest medial deltoid activity of the exercises tested (Campos 2020); a neutral humerus ("thumbs forward") gave the highest medial deltoid activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Main mover. The lateral raise gave the highest medial deltoid activity of the exercises tested (Campos 2020); a neutral humerus ("thumbs forward") gave the highest medial deltoid activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Helps, more so if the arm drifts forward or the thumb turns up (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Helps, more so if the arm drifts forward or the thumb turns up (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps lift the arm; the lateral raise also gave the highest posterior deltoid activity of the exercises tested (Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps lift the arm; the lateral raise also gave the highest posterior deltoid activity of the exercises tested (Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade near the top; shrugging adds more trapezius and less deltoid (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade near the top; shrugging adds more trapezius and less deltoid (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Keep the trunk from leaning away from the dumbbell (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Keep the trunk from leaning away from the dumbbell (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Out to the side, thumb forward
